text:
maria: Heads-up - a customer hit 401s after bundling our TypeScript SDK with Rollup + terser. They only see failures in prod bundle, local dev OK.
sam: thanks — do we have repro steps from the customer?
maria: yep, they pasted a minimal repro. Code: `import Redwood from '@redwood/inference'` then `client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.RW_KEY })` -> fetch returns 401 after bundle.
sam: any host/runtime? node vs edge?
maria: Node 18.16 in their CI, but they bundle for browser/edge target (they ship a single bundle to lambda-like host). They suspect tree-shaking
dev-jay: can you paste package.json and rollup config?
maria: pasted below:
```
// package.json (relevant)
{
  "name": "customer-app",
  "type": "module",
  "exports": {
    "./*": "./dist/*",
    "default": "./dist/browser/index.js"
  }
}
```
```
// rollup.config.js (relevant)
export default {
  input: 'src/main.ts',
  plugins: [nodeResolve({ browser: true }), commonjs(), terser()],
  output: { format: 'esm', sourcemap: true }
}
```
elaine: interesting — exports map default points to browser build. bundlers will prefer that and pull browser entry which includes our fetch wrapper for web environments.
maria: customer says the bundled code removes Authorization header before sending. They see `fetch` call with headers only in source, but in bundle `Authorization` is missing.
dev-jay: do we have a browser wrapper that strips headers? I vaguely remember we added a safety step to avoid leaking creds to cross-origin requests.
eng-ryan: yes. In the browser adapter we call `sanitizeHeaders()` to drop Authorization when credentials might leak to third-party origins. That code should not be used in Node runtime.
sam: so bundler picked browser entry for a server-targeted runtime due to exports map + nodeResolve({ browser: true }) -> picks browser field.
maria: customer workaround: change rollup nodeResolve to `browser: false` fixes it. But they can't always change build pipeline.
dev-jay: short-term: advise them to pin import to node entry: `import Redwood from '@redwood/inference/dist/node/index.js'` — ugly but works.
eng-ryan: long-term: we should update our package exports to include conditional exports: `{"node": "./dist/node/index.js", "import": "./dist/node/index.mjs", "browser": "./dist/browser/index.js"}` so bundlers target sensibly.
elaine: also we should publish a patch that moves sanitization behind a runtime detection check (prefer NODE_ENV or globalThis.fetch && !isNode).
deploy-bot: deploy queued: patch branch fix/exports-node-conditional -> CI build started :rocket:
maria: customer also reported types got dropped in their bundle (they relied on .d.ts from root import). We should ensure types field points to node types too.
sam: actionable: 1) send customer workaround (pin node entry or change rollup config) 2) ship patch that adds conditional exports + runtime guard around sanitizeHeaders + update types. 3) release 1.8.3 with notes.
eng-ryan: debugging note: we reproduced by setting `nodeResolve({ browser: true })` and bundling; rollup replaced our node adapter with browser shim. Confirmed header stripping is from `sanitizeHeaders`.
maria: I'll send repro steps + suggested workaround to the customer and mark for escalation. Thanks all :heart:
sam: created support ticket RW-5321 and marked eng-priority. :thumbsup:
